claims.evidence: The witness confirms it is an LG CRT television; the seller admits it is scrap.
The witness saw the screen dark and off.

claims.claim: No dead pixel, no line on the screen
claims.evidence: The TV was not shown powered on.
The remote control was not shown in the report.
Internal repair history cannot be determined from photos.

risks.risk: The cathode ray tube (CRT) may be burnt out or physically cracked.
risks.proof: A video of the TV powered on showing a clear image or static.
risks.if_unproven: As a non-functional unit for scrap/parts only.

risks.risk: The copper yoke or internal components may have been scavenged.
risks.proof: A photo of the rear panel with the casing intact and a photo of the model sticker.

risks.risk: The remote control may be missing or non-functional.
risks.proof: A photo of the remote control next to the TV.

proof_requests: Photo of the rear sticker showing the model number and manufacture date.
Photo of the back of the TV to confirm the casing is sealed.
Video of the TV plugged in and powered on, even if the image is distorted.
response.reason: The item is identified as an LG CRT and the seller explicitly declares it as non-functional scrap, which allows for a valuation based on its worst-case scrap/parts value.
